q: Two flutes play at the same time notes with the frequencies $440\,\text{Hz}$ and $437\,\text{Hz}$. What does a listener hear?
a: One sound whose pitch corresponds to a frequency of about $438.5\,\text{Hz}$ and whose loudness waxes and wanes: $f_\text{H} = |440\,\text{Hz} - 437\,\text{Hz}| = 3\,\text{Hz}$, that is, three loud moments per second.

q: The same echo measurement is made on a hot summer day and in a winter frost. On which occasion does the echo return sooner, and why?
a: On the hot summer day. In a gas the speed of sound increases as the temperature rises, in air by about $0.6\,\text{m/s}$ for every degree Celsius, so in warm air sound covers the same distance in a shorter time.
